name: Alber New
classification_notes: Clean geometric letterforms with a touch of humanist warmth in the curves place it as a geometric sans rather than a strict grotesque.
summary: A geometric sans built for brand voice work, clean enough for text and confident enough for headlines.
description: Alber New pairs plain geometric skeletons with just enough warmth in the curves to avoid feeling cold. Four weights with italics cover the usual brand range from body copy to display. It's a dependable, general-purpose choice rather than a typeface with a strong personality of its own.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes Alber New as a modern sans-serif combining clean geometry with subtle warmth, built for a confident and contemporary brand voice that works seamlessly from headlines to body text.

name: Alwyn New
classification_notes: A squared-off structure with an industrial edge marks this as a grotesque variant rather than a neutral geometric sans.
summary: A squarish, structured grotesque with an industrial edge, redrawn from Moretype's earlier release.
description: Alwyn New takes a squared-off skeleton and tightens the spacing and detailing for a more confident, structured finish. Five weights with italics move comfortably from wayfinding to editorial headlines. There's a rounded sibling if the industrial edge needs softening.
foundry_blurb: Moretype calls Alwyn New a modern sans-serif with a distinctive squarish structure, redesigned with improved spacing for brands wanting a confident, structured identity with a subtle industrial edge.

name: Alwyn New Rounded
classification_notes: Same squarish grotesque skeleton as Alwyn New but with rounded terminals, which softens it into a friendlier rounded sans.
summary: The rounded cut of Alwyn New, softening its squarish structure into a friendlier voice.
description: Alwyn New Rounded keeps the parent family's squared geometric bones but rounds off the terminals, trading some of the industrial edge for approachability. Five weights and italics carry over from the original. Good for brands that want structure without feeling stern.
foundry_blurb: Moretype presents this as a contemporary sans-serif that softens Alwyn New's structured, squarish form with smooth, rounded terminals for a friendlier brand voice.

name: Bale
classification_notes: Generous proportions and angled terminals give this a friendlier grotesque character rather than a neutral or geometric reading.
summary: A generously proportioned sans with angled terminals, warm enough for branding without losing structure.
description: Bale sits between clean and characterful: generous x-height and proportions with distinctive angled terminals give it a bit of personality without tipping into display territory. Five weights with italics handle branding and editorial work. A monospaced sibling, Bale Mono, extends the family into technical contexts.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes Bale as a contemporary sans-serif blending warmth and confidence in a clean, structured form, refined yet approachable for brands wanting consistency and a quietly distinctive edge.

name: Bale Mono
classification_notes: A fixed-width version of Bale's grotesque structure, so it's classified as mono rather than sans-serif.
summary: A monospaced cut of Bale, keeping its warmth but adding a grid-based, technical rhythm.
description: Bale Mono transposes the parent family's warmth into a fixed-width grid, aimed at code, data and system-driven interfaces that still want some personality. Five weights with italics match the Bale range. Useful where a plain monospace would feel too clinical.
foundry_blurb: Moretype pitches Bale Mono as a contemporary monospaced sans-serif adding a precise, technical edge to Bale's warm professionalism, for digital and data-driven environments.

name: Depot New
classification_notes: Sturdy, utilitarian proportions place this as an industrial grotesque, reworked from a 2006 original.
summary: A sturdy, industrial-feeling grotesque reworked from Moretype's 2006 original.
description: Depot New keeps the dependable, slightly blunt character of the original 2006 release but reworks spacing, kerning and features for modern use. Five weights with italics, plus new Thin styles, take it from bold headlines to legible body text. A condensed cut is available for tighter layouts.
foundry_blurb: Moretype calls Depot New a robust, contemporary sans-serif combining industrial strength with refined modernity, fully reworked from its 2006 release for brands wanting a dependable, utilitarian voice.

name: Depot New Condensed
classification_notes: The narrow-width companion to Depot New, keeping the same industrial grotesque character in a space-saving form.
summary: The condensed cut of Depot New, keeping its sturdy character in a tighter, more efficient form.
description: Depot New Condensed narrows the parent family's proportions without losing legibility, aimed at signage and layouts where space is tight. Same five weights and italics as the standard cut. A practical rather than showy choice.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes it as a space-efficient extension of Depot New, bringing the same sturdy, industrial character in a tighter, more compact form for functional signage work.

name: Faricy New
classification_notes: Clean geometry with subtle character places this as a general brand-oriented grotesque rather than a neutral workhorse.
summary: A polished, brand-ready sans that balances clean geometry with a touch of character.
description: Faricy New refines an earlier design into a system suited to identity work, with improved spacing and kerning over the original. Four weights with italics cover expressive headlines through to legible body copy. Solid rather than flashy.
foundry_blurb: Moretype frames Faricy New as a contemporary sans-serif refined into a polished, brand-ready system balancing clean geometry with subtle character.

name: Hedley New
classification_notes: Structured geometry with humanist touches in the curves places this closer to a humanist grotesque than a strict geometric sans.
summary: A modern sans mixing structured geometry with humanist touches for a confident, approachable voice.
description: Hedley New redesigns an earlier release with tighter spacing and a smoother rhythm across its four weights and italics. It reads as confident without feeling cold, which suits both bold headlines and readable body text. A dependable mid-weight choice for identity work.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes Hedley New as a modern sans-serif blending clean, structured geometry with subtle humanist touches for a confident yet approachable brand voice.

name: Hyla
classification_notes: Bold, exaggerated, single-weight forms built purely for attention-grabbing headline use place this squarely as a display face.
summary: A vibrant, single-weight display face built for shouting rather than reading.
description: Hyla is a headline-only typeface with exaggerated, bouncy forms that grab attention fast. There's no italic or additional weight, which keeps it firmly in the specialist display bracket. Best kept to packaging, posters and short bursts of copy.
foundry_blurb: Moretype calls Hyla a vibrant display typeface with playful, bold lines that instantly grab attention, ideal for headlines, packaging and advertising.

name: Mic 32 New
classification_notes: A futuristic, technical character with distinctive detailing marks this as a techno-leaning grotesque rather than a neutral sans.
summary: A futuristic revival with a distinctive techno character, reworked for cleaner spacing and wider use.
description: Mic 32 New reimagines an older design with cleaner kerning and expanded OpenType support while keeping its techno-leaning character intact. Four weights with italics suit brands after a digital, cutting-edge feel. Rounded and stencil siblings extend the family for display use.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes Mic 32 New as a futuristic sans-serif revival that reimagines the original Mic32 with cleaner spacing and expanded features while keeping its distinctive techno character.

name: Mic 32 New Rounded
classification_notes: Rounded terminals on the Mic 32 New skeleton push this toward display use, softening the parent's technical edge for headline and logo work.
summary: The rounded cut of Mic 32 New, softening its futuristic forms for friendlier headline use.
description: Mic 32 New Rounded keeps the parent's futuristic bones but rounds the terminals for a warmer take on the same techno structure. Four weights with italics suit headlines and logotypes rather than body text. A display companion rather than a standalone text face.
foundry_blurb: Moretype positions Mic 32 New Rounded as a contemporary display typeface adding a friendly, approachable edge to the original's futuristic forms, ideal for bold, confident identities.

name: Mic 32 New Stencil
classification_notes: Segmented, stencil-cut letterforms built for visual impact rather than running text place this in the display category.
summary: A stencil-cut version of Mic 32 New, trading legibility at small sizes for industrial visual impact.
description: Mic 32 New Stencil segments the family's futuristic geometry into a bold stencil form, aimed squarely at headlines and signage rather than text. Four weights with italics keep it flexible for display use. Distinctive rather than neutral.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes it as a modern display typeface combining futuristic geometry with a bold stencil aesthetic, giving brands an industrial-inspired voice.

name: Rehn
classification_notes: Balanced proportions with subtle humanist detailing across a wide weight range place this as a contemporary humanist sans.
summary: A clean, contemporary sans with a wide weight range and a condensed sibling for tighter layouts.
description: Rehn covers six weights from Thin to ExtraBold with matching italics, giving it more range than most of Moretype's other families. Balanced proportions and subtle detailing suit both branding and editorial use. A condensed cut is available where space is limited.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes Rehn as a clean, contemporary sans-serif with refined, modern construction and subtle humanist touches, versatile across branding, editorial and digital use.

name: Rehn Condensed
classification_notes: The narrow-width companion to Rehn, retaining its humanist detailing in a more compact form.
summary: The condensed cut of Rehn, bringing the same clarity into a narrower, space-efficient form.
description: Rehn Condensed narrows the parent family's proportions for dense layouts without sacrificing the humanist warmth of the original. Same six weights and italics as the standard cut. Suited to dynamic branding where space is at a premium.
foundry_blurb: Moretype describes it as a sleek, modern sans-serif bringing the clarity of Rehn into a narrower, space-efficient form for dynamic branding where impact and economy matter.

name: Varly
classification_notes: Organic, hand-drawn strokes and a single informal style place this in the script category rather than display sans.
summary: A lively, hand-drawn script with organic strokes built for a personal, informal brand voice.
description: Varly leans on visibly hand-drawn strokes and playful proportions rather than technical precision, which suits packaging and social contexts wanting warmth over polish. Single weight, no italic. Not a text face by any stretch.
foundry_blurb: Moretype calls Varly a lively, hand-drawn typeface that brings warmth and personality to a brand, ideal for packaging, social media and creative identities that want to feel personal.
